A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their main text, equations, figures, tables and complete appendices are readable and support reliable matching, including the additions in v3.

before.justification: v2 reports original experiments on trace generation, synthetic-data utility, instruction following and downstream prediction and infilling, with additional evaluations in Appendix D.

after.justification: v3 retains those original results and adds QwQ-32B trace-generation results and experiments on batch-job traces in Appendices D.6–D.7.

M1.justification: The text encoding, recursive generation, autoregressive training and instruction-tuning procedures remain unchanged. TraceLLM becomes the explicit model name; the batch-job experiment applies the existing approach without specifying a new algorithmic component.

E1.justification: Appendix D.7 adds training and evaluation on Alibaba 2018 cluster batch-job traces, representing task dependencies and resource requirements. This substantively extends empirical coverage beyond microservice communications to another workload domain. Existing Alibaba v2022 microservice tasks remain.

E2.justification: Appendix D.6 newly evaluates QwQ-32B and compares its trace-generation accuracy with TraceLLM's reported results. Existing comparator memberships remain unchanged. The batch-job experiment reuses GReaT, labeled Baseline in Figure 17.

E3.justification: Two focused protocols are added. QwQ uses two prompt examples and 10 samples per edge-count/depth pair, covering 2–10 edges and depths 2–5. Batch-job evaluation trains Llama-3.2 3B on 0.5B tokens and uses 1,000 cases per depth across depths 1–8. Existing experimental settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Figure 17 adds a depth-sensitivity comparison for batch-job traces, examining how validity changes for flat GReaT and recursive generation as DAG depth increases. Existing instruction ablations, temperature and model-size studies, and memorization analyses are retained.

E5.justification: The 20-run heavy-hitter evaluation, five-run evaluation with varying seeds in Section 4.3, and existing error bars remain unchanged. The additions report sample counts and accuracies without introducing new repeated-run or uncertainty-estimation practices.

E6.justification: Table 3 adds QwQ accuracies of 11.11%, 32.5%, 37.14% and 33.33% at depths 2–5. Figure 17 adds batch-job results with a reported recursive advantage of up to 47 percentage points. Existing microservice results are unchanged. QwQ uses different settings from Figure 3b, limiting direct performance comparisons.

T1.justification: The graph encodings, recursive probability factorization and Appendix C constraints remain unchanged. No new formal assumptions, mathematical derivations or proofs are introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the main claims about recursive trace generation, synthetic-data utility and downstream adaptation. Explicitly naming TraceLLM does not redefine these contributions, and broader applicability was already claimed in v2.

C2.justification: The limitations replace an open evaluation question about other trace types with a reference to the batch-job experiment and add a possible world-model role for agent development. D.6 interprets QwQ results as motivation for specialized trace modeling. Earlier limitations concerning discarded history and manually constructed instructions remain.

D1.justification: v3 documents the new QwQ prompt construction and the batch-job dataset, task attributes, model and training-token budget. Existing hardware, LoRA hyperparameters, preprocessing, inference settings and code-access information remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v3 adds references to Guo et al. (2019) for batch-job data, Qwen Team (2025) for QwQ-32B, and Kimi Team et al. (2025) for the world-model discussion. The established related-work coverage and novelty positioning otherwise remain stable.

P1.justification: v3 revises opening passages to introduce TraceLLM explicitly and clarify the training stages, updates affiliations, adds acknowledgments, and changes the numbered Limitations section into a run-in heading. Most existing prose and section organization are retained.

P2.justification: v3 adds Table 3 and Figure 17. Existing Figures 1–16 and Tables 1–2 retain their content and displays. Header changes, removed page-number footers and text reflow produce limited layout changes.

improvement.justification: The batch-job experiment provides useful empirical support for applying the approach beyond microservices, which v2 asserted without evaluating another trace domain. The gain is bounded: existing results and methods remain unchanged, the QwQ comparison uses different settings, and the proposed world-model application remains untested.
